reason: The arithmetic checks out and the defect is real, but the proposed fix is not. fixture.js pins TODAY = 2026-07-16 and the nearest live dated item is demo-audience-item-menu on 2026-08-01, so F.daysTo returns exactly 16 (15 days to 31 July, plus one). render-b.js line 49 prints "Nothing is planned for the next " + 16 + " days." Read the way anyone reads it, the next 16 days are 17 July to 1 August inclusive, and 1 August is precisely the day the menu tasting falls on. The honest empty span is 15 days. So the sentence is false by one, not acceptable as written. Driving the master confirms it renders on owner-flight, phone, desk, owner-editing and print, and that the collision is visible rather than theoretical: at desk and owner-flight the note sits at top=496 with the first item at top=467, so "Nothing is planned for the next 16 days." is level with a tick reading "16 | Menu tasting at The Orchard | SAT 1 AUG", and both sit under "Today is 16 July" where 16 means a third thing. Neither gate covers this: interaction-check.mjs asserts only that each tick's number equals FIXTURE.daysTo, and audit.mjs never reads copy, so this is not a restatement. On a direction whose entire claim is that a pixel is an honest unit of time, and on a string that prints on the A4 keepsake, a sentence that contradicts the tick beside it is a real 9.5-bar defect. The fix as written is refused. "Next: Menu tasting at The Orchard, Saturday 1 August." is direction C's thesis - lock.md lists "leading the received artifact with the single next thing, rather than making a reader find it on the measure" as the rejected idea from C - and the lock states plainly that in B "what is next is a filled tick and the nearest item", the measure and not a sentence. It would also print the title and date of the first item three lines above the tick that already carries the title and date of the first item, trading an off-by-one for a duplicate. The note must stay a statement about the gap.
sharpenedFix: Keep the sentence about the absence and make it true by construction rather than by a corrected count. In render-b.js line 49, drop the day count and state the boundary: "Nothing is planned until " + F.fmt.medium(ahead()[0].date) + "." which renders "Nothing is planned until 1 August." That is true under every reading, it cannot drift off by one when the fixture date moves, it clears the second 16 out from under "Today is 16 July", and it leaves what is next to the measure exactly as the lock requires - the note names the emptiness, the tick names the thing. If the founder wants the count form kept, do not inline the subtraction in the renderer: fixture.js already states that no surface may do its own arithmetic, so add a gapDays accessor returning daysTo(next) - 1 and render "Nothing is planned for the next 15 days." from it. Either way the string changes on all surfaces at once, since horizon() is shared by phone, desk, owner-flight, owner-editing and print.
